summary.title: Moving Blazingly Fast With The Core Vim Motions
summary.one_liner: You learn the core Vim cursor motions (word, character find, line, paragraph, search, counts, and semantic jumps) for fast, precise movement, shown in VSCodeVim.
keywords: how to move faster in vim
vim gg g go to line
takeaways: Word motions (w, b, e, ge) move by words, while capitalized WORD motions (W, B, E, gE) skip over punctuation for faster movement across code.
f and t jump to or just before a character on the line; ; and , repeat the last character search.
Search with /pattern and ?pattern, then use n and N to repeat the search; * and # search for the word under the cursor.
Prefix a motion with a count (for example 5j or 2w) to repeat it; keep counts for short jumps.
Use gd and gf for semantic jumps to a definition or an imported file, and gg, G, % for file and bracket navigation.
summary.summary: This tutorial, part of a VSCodeVim series, explains Vim motions for moving the cursor quickly and precisely. It covers word and WORD motions, character find and till motions, line and paragraph movements, search-based jumps, counts, and semantic motions like gd and gf. Each section gives short examples and when to use each motion, and the page ends with a summary of how the motions fit together and a pointer to operators.
